I couldn't read any file contents, so this diagnosis rests on the file names and my memory of this boilerplate's usual structure. The line numbers are estimates.

The most likely cause is `AuthService.resetPassword` in `src/auth/auth.service.ts`. In this boilerplate, that method is meant to delete the user's sessions after it saves the new password. That deletion is probably missing, or it deletes the wrong sessions. If so, the phone's session row survives the reset. The refresh token is validated against that session, so the phone can keep renewing its login.

The other two candidates are the session service and repository, which would be where a delete-by-user method is implemented incorrectly (for example a wrong filter).

candidates.explanation: After the reset hash is verified, the method sets the new password and saves the user. It does not delete the user's existing sessions (`sessionService.deleteByUserId({ userId: user.id })`). The phone's session row stays valid, so its refresh token still passes the session check in `refreshToken` and gets a new access token. Resetting the password should revoke every session for that user.

This is the helper `resetPassword` should call to revoke all of a user's sessions. If it is missing, or does not delete by user id, the reset cannot sign out other devices. This is less likely than the missing call in `resetPassword`.
If the repository's delete-by-user query is wrong (for example, it filters on the wrong column), sessions survive even when the service calls it. This is the least likely of the three.

fix.description: In AuthService.resetPassword, after loading the user and setting the new password, call `await this.sessionService.deleteByUserId({ userId: user.id });`. Then save the user with `usersService.update`. This invalidates every existing session, so refresh tokens on other devices fail the session lookup and those devices are signed out.

candidates.explanation: After the reset hash is verified, the method sets the new password and saves the user. It does not delete the user's existing sessions (`sessionService.deleteByUserId({ userId: user.id })`). The phone's session row stays valid, so its refresh token still passes the session check in `refreshToken` and gets a new access token. Resetting the password should revoke every session for that user.

This is the helper `resetPassword` should call to revoke all of a user's sessions. If it is missing, or does not delete by user id, the reset cannot sign out other devices. This is less likely than the missing call in `resetPassword`.
If the repository's delete-by-user query is wrong (for example, it filters on the wrong column), sessions survive even when the service calls it. This is the least likely of the three.

fix.description: In AuthService.resetPassword, after loading the user and setting the new password, call `await this.sessionService.deleteByUserId({ userId: user.id });`. Then save the user with `usersService.update`. This invalidates every existing session, so refresh tokens on other devices fail the session lookup and those devices are signed out.
